summary: Clackamas County, OR station with a 1937 100-ft crow's nest and later steel towers; register says gone; sources disagree on the steel tower's date (1940 vs 1957).

facts.design: 140-foot steel tower erected 1957 at the North Fork headquarters (district report); the register describes an earlier 100-foot twin tree crow's nest from 1937
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com both say it is gone; neither gives a removal date

staffing.status: no named lookout found; a 1959 item says an electric lift carried lookouts up and down a tower near Molalla, which the page does not tie to North Fork

events.note: Telephone line run from Molalla to the ranger cabin at North Fork Station (Molalla Pioneer item quoted on Forest Lookouts)
Steel tower on district headquarters property (register; firelookout.com); the district report dates a steel tower to 1957 instead
140-foot steel tower erected at North Fork Station per the Clackamas-Marion district annual report; conflicts with the register's 1940
Platforms and railings completed on the 140-foot tower; electric manlift installed instead of a safety rail
Registered August 26, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com date the steel tower to 1940. The Clackamas-Marion district annual report, quoted on Forest Lookouts, says a 140-foot tower was erected at North Fork Station in 1957. The story reports both dates and does not choose between them. The 1959 and 1961 Molalla items describe a 145-foot tower the page does not link to North Fork.

sources.title: North Fork Station Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Dates conflict: register and firelookout.com say a 100-foot crow's nest in 1937 and a steel tower in 1940; the Forest Lookouts page's district annual reports say a 140-foot steel tower was erected in 1957. The brief's height_m 42.7 (140 ft) matches the 1957 tower, not the register's 1937 crow's nest (100 ft); the design field says so. The 145-foot Molalla tower in the 1959 and 1961 items may or may not be this one; the story does not link it. Staffing: no named lookout found. Access: no source found, so no access fact is recorded. Removal date: not found. Oregon Department of Forestry records (CCC-era lookout blueprints and inventories, mentioned in an Oregon State Archives guide surfaced by search) might settle the dates; not read.
